UNDERWRITING GUIDELINES – Revised November 2023
UNDERWRITING GUIDELINES HOMEOWNERS FORMS HOA & HOA PLUS
GENERAL
• Home must show pride of ownership and proper maintenance.
• Home must be protected with smoke detectors in close proximity of sleeping areas and kitchen
areas.
• Porches or decks more than 2 feet off the ground or with 4 or more steps leading to them must

be protected with properly installed handrails meeting appropriate ordinances and state codes.
• Homes located in a Special Flood Hazard Area (Zone A or V) must be covered by a Federal
Flood insurance policy with matching building limit (or maximum available).
• All Risks in Territories 08X, 09X, 10X must exclude wind.
• An inspection is required on homes over 5 years old.
INELIGIBLE RISKS
• Homes with wood, flat (unless in and around El Paso), asbestos, tar/gravel, expensive metal,

corrugated metal, concrete or clay tile roofs (unless a High Value Home) and slate roofs, both
real and artificial slate are unacceptable.
• Town homes, duplexes, unless meeting Single Building definition.
• Homes located on more than 1 acre (require Underwriter approval).
• Unprotected property not visible from another dwelling and not located on an all weather road.
• Home located more than 5 miles from an ISO-rated responding fire department.
• Homes in foreclosure.

• Homes in foreclosure.
• Mobile homes; manufactured homes.
• Homes of unconventional construction including log, do-it-yourself, dome, shell homes; using
unconventional parts; not meeting building codes.
• Commercial risks or properties converted to private dwellings.
• Apartment Houses.
• Properties located entirely over water on piers or stilts.
• Homes with aluminum wiring.
• Homes with space heaters. Space heaters as supplemental to a thermostatically controlled

central heating system are acceptable if not using fossil fuels.
• Homes in First Tier Territories with Windstorm coverage.
• Homes within 1,000 feet of the Gulf of Mexico or any coastal bay.
• Homes with swimming pools, spas or hot tubs that are not properly secured. Pools secured by a
6’ high fence with locked or self locking gates are acceptable.
• Diving boards and slides are not eligible. A maximum of $100,000 personal liability is

provided for approved pools ($300,000 for High Value Homes).
• Seasonal, unoccupied, or vacant homes. If ARI insures the primary home, refer any
seasonal/secondary dwelling unbound to the underwriter for consideration.
• Homes with Asbestos Siding.
• Homes with open foundations.

APPLICANT
• Must hold title to home with a maximum of two mortgages.
CREDIT HISTORY
• Credit is evaluated along with prior claims history, condition of property, age of property, and
other risk factors.
INSURANCE TO VALUE
• Risks must be insured for ACV of at least 80% of replacement cost.
• HOA-Plus or Replacement Cost on Coverage A: risks must be insured for at least 100% of
replacement cost. Agent must use judgment in evaluating ACV. Appraisals or sales

transactions provide excellent evidence of ACV with adjustment for land value.
OCCUPANCY/USE
Residence must be:
• Owner occupied by owner’s immediate family.
• Occupied at least 9 months per year.
• Used for private residential purposes only. Coverage for business property/pursuits is limited
under Section 1 and excluded from Section 2.
SECONDARY/SEASONAL RESIDENCES
• A dwelling occupied by owner for less than 9 months per year is considered seasonal. Seasonal

residences are not eligible for coverage in this program unless ARI insures the primary home and
only then if prior underwriting approval is given by the underwriter to insure the seasonal home.
ELECTRICAL, PLUMBING, HEATING AND ROOF
• Homes must be in very good condition. The Wiring/Electrical Service, Plumbing, Heating and
Roof must meet the requirements outlined below.

HOA Underwriting Guidelines 11/3/2023

American Risk Insurance Company
• Wiring/Electrical Service: 100 amp service, and all switches, fixtures must meet code. Breaker
boxes are required. Aluminum, knob and tube wiring and fuses are unacceptable.
• Plumbing: Exposed water lines (must be copper or PVC), plumbing fixtures and hot water
storage tank must meet code. Galvanized, mixed-galvanized or lead plumbing are not
acceptable.
ROOF
• All roofs must be in good condition regardless of age. Normal wear and granule loss. No

evidence of blistering, cracking, cupping/curling, defective materials or installation, missing
shingles, tree damage or tree limbs greater than 2.5 inches overhanging the roof.
• Maximum of 1 overlay of composition shingles over composition (over wood ineligible)
shingles.
• Metal roofs must be pre approved by Underwriting.
• Metal roofs must include the Non-Structural Hail Loss Limitation Endorsement.
• All eaves and roof vents inspected to ensure proper condition, operation and adequacy.

• Must have 5 years or more remaining useful life.
• Roofs that are 15 years or older will be covered on an Actual Cash Value (ACV) basis.
HEATING AND COOLING SYSTEMS
• Primary heating/cooling system must be a thermostatically controlled, central system.
• Thermostatically controlled space heaters are acceptable only as secondary heating sources.
Kerosene, coal, wood or solar as a source of fuel is unacceptable.
LOSS HISTORY

LOSS HISTORY
Claims are evaluated as part of the underwriting process. Unacceptable prior loss history:
• Two or more Act of Nature claims reported within past 5 years.
• One or more All Other Losses* within past 3 years.
• Two or more All Other Losses* within the past 5 years.
• Total of Two or more losses under $15,000 in 3 years.
• Total of Three or more losses under $15,000 in past 5 years.
*All Other Losses are losses other than water, fire, theft or liability. A prior mold loss will

require evidence of remediation to be acceptable.
Contact Underwriting, do not bind:
• One or more water, fire, theft or liability losses in the past 5 years. (If approved, the loss will
count as one loss in determining if the total losses are acceptable).
• One or more losses with a payout of $15,000 or more within 5 years.

Claims with prior water-damage losses are evaluated in accordance with Subchapter C, Chapter 5,
Articles 5.354 of the Texas Insurance Code and related regulations, including §21.1007 of the
Texas Administrative Code.
A homeowner’s policy may be surcharged at the time the policy is renewed for non weather related
claims that are paid by the company as follows:
• 5% surcharge if the insured has filed two or more claims in the preceding policy year.

• An additional 3% surcharge may be added if the insured files an additional claim in the policy
year following the year of the initial surcharge.
• 10% surcharge if the insured has filed three or more claims under the policy in a three year
period.
• The total premium surcharge may not exceed 10% of the total policy premium.
BINDING AUTHORITY
• Agents may bind risks up to the maximum allowed dwelling value without contacting

Underwriting. Agents have 24-hour binding authority. Risk may be written up to 30 days prior
to effective date.
• Risk must meet the Eligibility/Underwriting guidelines. Any risk not meeting the guidelines
but judged by the agent to be a good risk may be referred to Underwriting before binding.
• HOA(+) Binding Limit: $700,000 (Homes with values between $700,000 and $1,000,00 must
be submitted to Underwriting for approval)
PREVIOUS CANCELLATIONS OR NONRENEWALS

PREVIOUS CANCELLATIONS OR NONRENEWALS
• Risks previously canceled or non-renewed by another insurer must be referred to company
prior to binding.
HURRICANE, TROPICAL STORM, OR SEVERE WEATHER
• Agent’s binding authority automatically terminates for new business and coverage increases in
First and Second Tier Counties (Territories 01X, 08X, 09X, 10X, 11X) when a Hurricane or
Tropical Storm Watch or Warning has been issued by the National Weather Bureau within any

part of the Gulf of Mexico, or when a when a Hurricane or Tropical Storm enters the Gulf of
Mexico, or when a Hurricane or Tropical Storm is:
West of 80° W longitude and North of 20° N latitude
• Binding authority automatically terminates for any area placed under a Tornado or Severe
Weather Warning or Watch by the National Weather Bureau.
• This rule will not affect issuance of policies for business previously quoted and bound prior to

the weather warning being issued or with effective dates at least 10 days into the future.

CANCELLATION OR REDUCTIONS IN LIMITS OF LIABILITY OR COVERAGE

CANCELLATION OR REDUCTIONS IN LIMITS OF LIABILITY OR COVERAGE
• Mandatory coverage may not be canceled unless the entire policy is canceled.
• If insurance is increased or reduced, the additional or return premium shall be computed on a
prorate basis.
• Flat cancellations after the effective date will require proof of the other insurance (via
declarations page) and must be made within 30 days of effective date.
• The insured may cancel the policy at any time for any reason.

MULTIPLE COMPANY INSURANCE
• We will not provide coverage for a dwelling that is also covered by another insurance policy.
TRANSFER OR ASSIGNMENT
• No transfers or assignments are permitted. Each insured and/or property will require
submission of a new application.
SINGLE BUILDING DEFINITION
• Buildings that are separated by space shall be considered as separate buildings.

• Buildings or sections of buildings, which are separate buildings by a 6inch reinforced concrete
or 8inch masonry party wall that pierce or rises to the underside of the roof and pierces or
extends to the inner side of the exterior wall, shall be considered a separate building.
Accessibility between buildings with independent walls or through masonry party walls
described above shall be protected by at least a Class A Fire Door installed in a masonry wall
section.

Roofing must be in good condition and deemed acceptable by Underwriting at the time of inspection. Roof must have at
least 5 years life expectancy unless otherwise noted to be considered at time of New Business.
• Composite or Architectural Shingle Roofs should have ¾ of its life expectancy at the time of new business to qualify

for replacement cost coverage. Composite or Architectural Shingle Roofs are subject to require a Limited Loss
Settlement for Windstorm or Hail Losses to Roofing Surfacing endorsement to be eligible for New and Renewal

roofs should be completely replaced before the roof becomes 21 years old based on national statistics and

therefore are subject to inspection to determine if the conditions of the roof permit renewal of the policy.
• Tile and metal roofs should be 20 years of age or newer at the time of new business to qualify for replacement
cost coverage. Tile and metal roofs that are over 21 years old will require the Limited Loss Settlement for
Windstorm or Hail Losses to Roof Surfacing endorsement. Tile or metal roofs over 25 years old should be

completely replaced based on national statistics and therefore are subject to inspection to determine if the

An underwriting suspension, also called a moratorium, is a temporary suspension to agent and broker
binding authority for select lines of business due to a catastrophic natural event or other increased

threat of loss across a specified geographic area. During a suspension, we will not accept for any
of the designated geographic areas:
Applications for new coverage or endorsements for increased coverage
•
Requests to change deductibles on existing policies
•
Requests to change the insured location address on a policy
•
Requests for backdating transactions
•
Payment for lapsed policies.

Should a binding suspension be warranted, agents and brokers will be notified via the @Chubb Agent

lifted. Should agents and brokers have questions about suspensions, they can contact local
underwriting representatives. Chubb employees will be notified via company intranet regarding the
suspension.
IV. Unacceptable Risks Due To Claims Activity
Risk locations associated with claims activity as described below are ineligible for home insurance.

1. A risk shall be deemed ineligible if the applicant has had a liability claim that arose out of that
person's negligence during the previous three-year period.
2. A risk shall be deemed ineligible if the applicant has two or more non-weather, non-water
damage claims paid during the previous three-year period.
3. A risk shall be deemed ineligible if there has been three or more appliance related claims paid
within a three-year period to the applicant or at the risk location.

within a three-year period to the applicant or at the risk location.
4. A risk shall be deemed ineligible if there has been more than one water damage claim filed by
the applicant or on the risk to be insured.

5. A risk shall be deemed ineligible if there has been one water damage claim filed by the
applicant or on the risk to be insured and at least one other claim or any unacceptable
underwriting characteristic.
6. A risk shall be deemed ineligible if there has been a non-water paid claim of more than $50,000
within a five-year period to the applicant or on the risk to be insured. Two (2) or fewer
appliance-related claims; one (1) water loss; or any mold-related claims, which have been

properly remediated, are not considered.
Definitions applicable to these guidelines:
a. Appliance-related claim -- A request by an insured for indemnification from an insurer for a loss arising
from the discharge or leakage of water or steam from an appliance that is the direct result of the failure of
the appliance. An appliance includes air conditioning units, heating units, refrigerators, dishwashers,

icemakers, clothes washers, water heaters, and disposals. An appliance-related claim shall not include the
failure of a plumbing system or an external attachment to the appliance used to transport water to or from
the plumbing system. Appliance related claims are not considered when: (1) they have been properly
remediated and, (2) the remediation has been inspected and certified by a person or entity that is properly

licensed, knowledgeable and experienced in the remediation of water (see regulation for licensing details).
If the above criteria are not met, the appliance related claim will be considered a water damage claim.
b. Water damage claim--A request by an insured for indemnification from an insurer for a loss arising from
the discharge or leakage of water or steam that is the direct result of the failure of a plumbing system or

other system that contains water or steam. This also includes appliance related claims that do not satisfy
the criteria listed in a. above.
c. Mold claim -- Previous mold damage or mold related claim(s) either for a dwelling or applicant are not
considered for underwriting purposes if the property was:
i. Remediated in accordance with the requirements specified in Chapter 1958 Subchapter D of the
Occupations Code and any applicable rules promulgated by the Texas board of Health; and a

Certificate of Mold Damage Remediation is issued to the property owner order Section 1958.154 of
the Occupations Code; or
ii. Inspected by and independent mold assessor or adjuster, who is licensed to perform mold assessment
in accordance with rule promulgated by the Texas Board of Health under Chapter 1958 of the
Occupations Code, and the property owner is provided a written certification on a Certificate of Mold

Damage Remediation that based on the mold assessment inspection, the property does not contain
evidence of mold damage.
V. Renewal Guidelines
A risk may be moved by Chubb, at renewal to a tier for which it qualifies. Chubb will re-underwrite the
risk based on all the eligibility criteria outlined in the Homeowners Underwriting Rules Secs. I-III and in
compliance with all applicable Texas Insurance Codes, including §551.152 and §551.104. An agent can

also request placement in another writing company at renewal. A new application with updated
information should be submitted to Chubb by the insured’s agent or broker for underwriter review.

of non-renewal will be sufficient proof of notice.

a. These risks will be declined at New Business or cancelled within the underwriting
review period or are not eligible for renewal if the policy is in effect three (3)
years or less:
i. Risks with more than one non-weather loss.

ii. Risks with any non-weather loss that occurs within the underwriting review
period, excluding losses protected under Texas Insurance Code §544.353
(appliance-related water damage claims that have been properly remediated
and certified) or Texas Insurance Code §544.303 (mold-related claims where
remediation has been completed and evidenced as required).

iii. Risks with open claims.

iv. Any liability and/or fire claims.

iii. Risks with open claims.

iv. Any liability and/or fire claims.

b. Prior mold-related claims will not affect a consumer's eligibility for coverage or any
underwriting decision, provided all of the following conditions are met:

i. The applicant has property eligible for coverage under a residential property
insurance policy;
ii. The property has had prior mold damage;
iii. The mold damage has been remediated; and
iv. The remediation is evidenced by either:
e A Certificate of Mold Remediation issued under Texas Occupations

Code §1958.154, establishing with reasonable certainty that the
underlying cause of the mold has been remediated; or

e Aninspection by an independent assessor or adjuster who
determined, based on the inspection, that the property no longer
contains evidence of mold damage.

c. Wewill not consider a prior appliance-related water damage claim as a basis for any
underwriting decision — including the decision to issue, renew, cancel, or rate a policy
— provided the requirements of Texas Insurance Code §544.353(c) or §544.353(d), as
applicable, are satisfied. This prohibition applies to a maximum of two (2) such claims
per insured or per covered property within any three-year period. A third or

subsequent appliance-related claim within that same three-year period is not entitled
to protected status and may be considered in our underwriting decisions pursuant to
Texas Insurance Code §544.353(e).

d. Our decision to refuse to renew a policy is subject to the following conditions:

i. We will not consider the following claim types when determining whether to
refuse renewal:

e Claims resulting from a loss caused by natural causes;

e Claims that were filed but are not paid or payable under the policy;
or

e Appliance-related water damage claims we are prohibited from
using under Texas Insurance Code §544.353.

ii. We may refuse to renew a policy only if the insured has filed three (3) or more
claims under the policy within any three-year period, excluding the claim types
identified in section (i) above.

D. Older Homes/Age of Major Systems:

a. Dwellings 40 years and older will be written with the Limited Water Damage
Coverage endorsement (LWD) at a $10,000 limit. Higher sublimits may be
available, up to a maximum of 10% of Coverage A or $50,000, whichever is less.
Requests for removal of LWD will be determined based on, but not limited to, the
overall condition of the plumbing system, the condition of the home, and the age
and location of the risk. Proof of significant upgrades and renovations to current

plumbing standards will be required, and approval is subject to Underwriter
discretion.

b. Dwellings with fuses, cloth, double tap, knob and tube, or aluminum wiring are
not eligible.

c. Dwellings with Federal Pacific, Stab-lok, GTE Sylvania, Zinsco, Challenger
electrical panels are ineligible.

d. Dwellings must have electrical and plumbing systems that are in good condition
according to current standards. These systems will be reviewed for condition if
the property is 40+ years old unless the system in question has been updated in
the past 20 years.

e. Dwellings with evaporative cooling systems and/or without central air/heat are
not eligible.

f. HVAC units (condenser and air handler) older than 20 years will be reviewed for
eligibility. HVAC units (including the condenser and air handler) found to be in
poor condition will be deemed unacceptable.

g. Dwellings with Polybutylene, cast-iron and/or galvanized plumbing are not
eligible.

h. Dwellings with water heaters found to be in poor condition are unacceptable.
Water heaters will be reviewed for condition based upon age, as follows:

i. Ten (10) years or older if located inside the dwelling.
ii. Fifteen (15) years or older if located outside the dwelling/living area.

process the applicant information by using ForemostSTAR.com or by calling 1-800-527-3905 within these five days. Coverage is bound when the producer has advised the

customer of the effective date of coverage. Coverage may not be backdated, i.e., producers cannot make coverage effective prior to the date it was bound. PRIOR TO BINDING
COVERAGE, the producer must determine that the risk meets the underwriting criteria and all necessary documents must be obtained. Limitations on binding authority are in place

for all producers unless the producer has an amendment to the agency agreement detailing exceptions to their binding authority. Violation of binding authority will result in policy
cancellation.
Limits exceeding producer binding authority require Underwriting Approval and cannot be bound. Underwriting may require submission of supporting documentation.

We reserve the right to use judgment in evaluating your binding authority and can restrict or limit binding authority at our sole discretion for valid underwriting and business
reasons.
Important: For non-bound risks, coverage is not in-force until a policy is issued. If coverage has been bound, using the binding process described above, the producer must issue

the policy within the five-day binding period. If unable to issue the policy, the producer must notify the Company within the five days.

Eligibility Guidelines
Safeco is a Preferred Market where the quality of risk matters. We seek to insure responsible property owners who
practice prudent upkeep, carefully maintain their property and present the opportunity to write additional lines of
business. Our Landlord Protection® Product can be written monoline, but is best when packaged with all of a
customer's policies.

customer's policies.
We rely on our agents to underwrite the risks, confirm eligibility requirements are met and to ensure the property is
well maintained and occupied. A property insured under our Landlord Protection® program must be currently
occupied by a tenant. All structures on an individual parcel must be insured with Safeco.
Our Landlord Protection Product was built upon a history of disciplined underwriting, but even if a rate is offered, we

expect you, our agents, to practice disciplined front-line underwriting to determine if this is a customer that will enjoy a
long-term relationship with your agency and with us.
If you have a customer who has multiple property claims in the last five years, it's a good idea to call your underwriter
first to discuss the risk. While any customer may have that occasional mishap, we both want to enter into a

relationship with someone who is responsible, takes care of themselves and their property and pays their bills on
time. Generally speaking, if a property and customer are claims-free, or have a small incident in the last few years,
the property will likely be acceptable.

General Eligibility
Note: Items in bold are further defined in Section IV. Definitions and Reference Information
An eligible property risk is one which:
A. is well maintained, occupied, not unduly exposed to loss and is insured for an amount that is adequate to
reconstruct it at today's costs;
B. is tenant-occupied, used exclusively for private residential purposes, with no more than 4 units, each designed

for one-family occupancy
• Long term rentals, seasonal dwellings, and Short term rentals are considered eligible.
• Landlord Protection® forms 2 and 3 must be written at 100% Replacement Cost
• All losses in the prior 5 years are subject to underwriting review
Note: Seasonal dwellings and Short term rental properties must be rented in whole. We understand that some of
these properties are owner occupied at times, however to be eligible, they must be occupied by a tenant more often

than they are owner occupied. Short term and seasonal properties may not be occupied by the owner for more than
five consecutive months annually.
Buildings owned by a corporation, company or other legal entity are not eligible. Exceptions are available for trusts,
estates, LLC’s, LLP’s, LP’s which own private residential property for the benefit of an individual owner who is the
individual named insured on a Landlord Protection policy. The entity must have no other commercial activities.

Eligible trusts, estates, LLC’s, LLP’s, LP’s may be added as a second named insured or Additional Insured on the
policy.

Definitions and Reference Information
Coverage Declined, Cancelled or Non-Renewed During the Last five (5) Years
Acceptability of the risk dependent upon the reason for the coverage declination, cancellation or non-renewal.
In whole
The entire property is rented under one lease. The insured does not reside at the property while it is rented. In whole

rentals do not include rentals of part of the insured location such as a single room or outbuildings (i.e. renting an
above garage apartment and separate home to two different tenants). Eligible landlord properties will be rented in
whole.
Loss
All paid losses (including CAT losses), incurred in the last 5 years to the dwelling or personal possessions while in the
insured's ownership at this location only.
Non-Standard Buildings

insured's ownership at this location only.
Non-Standard Buildings
Underground homes, manufactured homes, houses built on pilings or stilts or built out of unusual, non-standard
materials.
Owner Occupied Property
A long term rental that is occupied by the owner. An example might be a multi-unit dwelling where the owner resides
in one unit. Owner occupied also means a Short term rental or Seasonal dwelling that is occupied by the owner

more often than it is tenant occupied or is occupied by the owner for more than five consecutive months annually.
Back to Table of Contents American Economy Insurance Company 9

®
Texas • Dwelling Fire: Landlord Protection Eligibility Guidelines
Seasonal dwelling
A property that is typically occupied on an intermittent basis for less than 6 months a year. Often, a seasonal rental
will be a short term rental.
Short term rental
One or more rentals of the insured location in whole, so long as it is not rented for more than 180 consecutive days to
the same person(s) during the policy period. Short term rental lease terms can vary (daily, weekly or monthly).

Tenant Occupied Property
A long term rental that is occupied by a tenant year round or a Short term rental or Seasonal dwelling that is
occupied by a tenant more often than it is owner occupied. Short term and seasonal properties may not be occupied
by the owner for more than five consecutive months annually.
Unoccupied
A residence is considered unoccupied if it is furnished but not occupied by tenants at the time coverage is bound.

Every unit in a multi-unit dwelling must be occupied. Short term and seasonal properties may be unoccupied at the
time coverage is bound. However, properties should not be unoccupied for more than 60 days.
Vacant
Any dwelling that is vacant (unfurnished and not currently occupied) at the time coverage is bound.

PREMIUM CALCULATION
Many policy variables and the rate classifications within each are used in developing the final premium. In general,
the factor for each rate class is multiplied by the factor for the rate class of the preceding variable. The following
variables and rate classifications are utilized in rating.

INSURANCE SCORE
The primary named insured's credit-based insurance score, combined with a named insured's Prior Liability Limit, is
included in the premium calculation.
Once the insurance score is determined at new business, it shall not change and shall be used for subsequent renewal
terms, unless a new insurance score is ordered and applied to the policy, as described below.

Insurance score will be re-ordered by the Company at every third renewal from the last order. Based on the new
insurance score, the policy will be updated.
At the request of the named insured, the Company shall re-order the insurance score and determine if the new score
would impact the policy. If the new score is a better score, the policy will be updated. If the new score is a worse
score, the policy will not be updated. However, the named insured may not make such a request more than once in

any 12-month period and any change in insurance score will be made at the policy's renewal.
If the applicant or named insured can prove that an extraordinary life event, such as catastrophic illness, temporary
loss of employment, divorce, death in family, military deployment overseas, etc. negatively impacted their insurance
score, the insurance score with that event will not be used to negatively impact the policy. This benefit must be

requested by or on behalf of the applicant or named insured.

PRO-RATA PREMIUM CALCULATION
